stem.en: The anthers of a flower are removed before they mature. Later, pollen from another plant of the same species is dusted onto its stigma, and seeds form. Which process has been ensured?

feedback.en: The flower has no anthers left, so it cannot give itself pollen.
Budding is a kind of asexual reproduction. Here pollen and seeds are involved.
Yes. The only pollen on the stigma came from another plant.
Tissue culture grows plants from tiny pieces in a nutrient medium, with no pollen.

explanation.en: Removing the anthers takes away the flower's own pollen. The pollen dusted on the stigma came from another plant of the same species, so this is cross-pollination.

hints.en: Where did the pollen on the stigma come from?
Could the flower have used its own anthers?
